sources.entry: Fader - Menu bar volume mixer with per-app volume, one-click output switching, and Bluetooth headphone control. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/pantafive/fader) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Fader - Menu bar volume mixer with per-app volume, one-click audio output switching, and Bluetooth headphone control.

summary.one_liner: Fader is a macOS menu bar app for switching audio output devices, setting per-app volume, and playing sound to several outputs at once.
summary.what_it_does: Fader lives in the macOS menu bar and lists audio outputs such as headphones, speakers, displays, and AirPlay targets, letting you switch between them with one click. It can connect paired Bluetooth headphones from the same list. Auto-switch follows a user-ranked list of devices and picks the highest-ranked one that is present. You can drag a device onto the Output section to play through several outputs together, each with its own slider. Per-app volume gives each app that plays sound a fader and mute button, with levels persisted; apps at full volume are passed through untouched. Per-app output routes chosen apps to specific devices, and the microphone section switches the default input, sets gain, and shows which apps are listening. System volume stays in sync with the volume keys and Control Center.
use_cases: switch headphones and speakers on a Mac
control volume separately for each app
play audio to several outputs at once
route one app to a different speaker
connect Bluetooth headphones from the menu bar
how_to_run: Or download the latest dmg from the project releases and open it
Development: brew install xcodegen swiftlint swiftformat
notable: No telemetry, no kernel extension, and no virtual audio driver, per the README
Per-app volume uses macOS audio taps; tapped audio stays on the Mac
Apps at full volume play untouched, bit-perfect
Source is MIT licensed and the README invites independent code review
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon
Per-app volume needs the System Audio Recording permission
Development requires Xcode project generation via XcodeGen; the .xcodeproj is not edited by hand
